messages:
Maria (PM): Quick sync — GA is locked to the date but not to the final feature set. I propose a formal 'swaplist' process so we can swap lower-risk v1 items into v1 if MVP items miss the freeze. Keeps customer value stable and reduces last-minute chaos. Thoughts?

Ben (Eng): Sounds useful. Need a strict definition of what can be swapped vs what must land in MVP. Also we need a standard format for the cutlist so on-call and release folks can parse it quickly.

AJ (Staff Eng): Agree. My suggested guardrails for swap candidates: no new infra dependencies, surface area <= 3 UI screens or equivalent API, and must include either automated tests or a mocked test harness. Otherwise QA time balloons.

Eve (Design): Designers need a 1 business-day buffer for any swapped item to handle copy/accessibility microfixes. If a feature swaps in the evening before GA, we need at least a small runway for content.

Sam (C-S): Two paying mid-market customers pushed for tenant routing + per-customer quotas. High ROI but large scope. Can we treat them as v1 unless a very small shim can satisfy them?

Maria (PM): Tenant routing & quotas = mark v1 by default. If Eng can propose a slim 'read-only routing config' or a config-only quota surface that avoids infra and UX work, we can consider as a swap candidate.

Taylor (Prod Ops): Operational constraint: feature-freeze is at 2332109800 UTC. For swaps to be actionable we need the final cutlist locked by 2332109000 (roughly 2.2 days before freeze) so we can plan releases and test windows. No ad-hoc roll-ins after freeze without exec sign-off.

Ben (Eng): I'll drop a CSV template for the cutlist. Minimal columns to keep it machine-readable: feature_id, owner, risk_level, infra_delta, est_eng_hours, qa_notes. Example snippet: ```feature_id,owner,risk_level,infra_delta,est_eng_hours,qa_notes
ROUTE-12,Ben,medium,no,24,"needs mock env"
KV-07,Me,high,yes,80,"infra + DB migration"
```

Maria (PM): Good. Also want a simple scoring rubric for swap decisions: customer_impact, dev_cost, regression_risk. We can add customer_count and revenue_signal as tiebreakers.

AJ (Staff Eng): Practical rule: if regression_risk > medium -> auto v1. No high-risk swaps allowed pre-freeze. Also require a canary plan + feature flag for anything swapped in near-GA.

Sam (C-S): I'll add the customer request details and revenue signals to the doc so scoring is data-driven.

Eve (Design): I'll prepare a 1-day content pass checklist (microcopy, aria labels, error states) and a rule for UX surface area classification (tiny/config/panel/full flow).

DeployBot: deploy-window-notice: Next full regression run scheduled 2332109400 UTC. Test env will be locked until results posted.

Taylor (Prod Ops): Action items: Ben -> CSV template + example by 2332110200; Maria -> draft scoring rubric + swaplist playbook; Eve -> content-pass checklist; Sam -> customer briefs added. I'll annotate the schedule constraints in the doc.

Ben (Eng): Uploaded CSV example to #prod-docs: https://redwood.internal/prod-docs/swaplist-example (link).

Maria (PM): Scheduling a 30-min triage tomorrow 10:30am PT to finalize initial cutlist. Inviteing @AJ @Ben @Eve @Taylor @Sam. If you can't attend, add notes/rows in the sheet.

Eve (Design): Quick Q: If a swap happens after freeze but before GA and it passes scoring, do we require a canary?

AJ (Staff Eng): Yes — canary + feature flag + explicit rollback steps. No exceptions unless exec approves with documented risk and test plan.

Maria (PM): Final rule draft: swap allowed only if scoring passes AND (no infra_delta AND canary + feature_flag) OR explicit executive sign-off with rollback plan.

Ben (Eng): Note: KV-cache work looks deceptively small but touches runtime paths — mark KV-cache related items medium-high risk unless scope is stripped.

Maria (PM): Marking KV-cache as default v1 unless a narrow shim is proposed.

Sam (C-S): This gives us a defensible path to keep the GA date while still being responsive to customer asks. Appreciate the alignment. :thumbsup:

Maria (PM): I'll publish the swaplist playbook and the first cutlist snapshot after the triage. Closing thread until the meeting.

Eve (Design): :+1:

AJ (Staff Eng): :thumbsup:

Taylor (Prod Ops): Will enforce the windows. If anyone pushes for late exec sign-off, include cost and SRE impact in the request.

Maria (PM): closing.
